title: review (other model, opus): D1 fix rounds on task/T-0157 — delta 2e32566..8a82703 (T-0151/T-0154, executed by claude:sonnet)
spec: Review the delta `git diff 2e32566 8a82703` in worktree wt/T-0157 (fix rounds T-0151 and T-0154 on top of the already-reviewed T-0120 commit, rebased onto goal/T-0109; files orchestrator/daemon.py, tests/test_daemon.py, .orchestrator/pool.toml, CLAUDE.md, .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md). It answers review T-0150; confirm each item resolved: (1) reviews_expected(t) used by gate() and merge_reviewed(); an orphaned complexity-7 task merges on one approve (test); (2) a failed or held sibling review holds the source task with hold_reason naming the sibling and notifies once, no unbounded wait (test); (3) second review never on the executor's model: Claude-executed → both reviews on the non-executing tier, the second carrying constraints.avoid_account and second_review; Codex-executed → tiers differ (test); docstring, pool.toml [review] comment and README paragraph say the same; (4) CLAUDE.md line, tests/test_daemon.py docstring and prompts/planner.md say 6 with the pool.toml pointer and test_planner_md_matches_claude_md_lists is green; (5) merged_at stamped on the source task before merge.merge. Also: `git diff 1b94384 2e32566 -- README.md .orchestrator/pool.toml` shows the T-0120 conflict resolution kept T-0121's scout limits and scouts line; reconcile_dead and the orphaned branch intact; no shell strings from config. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon tests.test_goals -q` once. Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments; keep to real defects.
acceptance: Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments
Each of the five T-0150 items confirmed resolved or named unresolved with evidence
Conflict resolution kept both D1 and D2 content

comments.issue: T-0150 item 2 only half-fixed. The failed/held-sibling escape hatch lives inside `for r in bus.read(status="done", role="review")`, so it only fires when at least one review reaches done with an approve. If BOTH reviews of a complexity-7 task fail (spawn.run_worker sets status='failed' on 'review returned no parseable verdict' - the exact T-0139/T-0135 mode, and a prompt/diff problem that fails one review usually fails its twin), merge_reviewed never iterates either of them: src stays status=done with gated_at stamped, gate() skips it forever, no hold, no hold_reason, no notify. Same for the single-review 4-6 path when its one review fails. That is the identical silent-stall class item 2 named. The sweep needs to be over done-but-unmerged execute tasks (or over all reviews of src, not just done ones), not over done reviews.

`avoid_account` is always None here, so the 'different account when possible' promise in pool.toml:26 and README.md:34 is never attempted. `existing[0]` is the snapshot bus.create_task returned three lines up - create_task (bus.py:92) sets assigned_to=None and no 'account' key at all, and it is never re-read - so `.get("account") or .get("assigned_to")` is None on every gate-created second review. Verified by running gate() on a complexity-7 claude:opus-executed task: constraints == {'avoid_account': None, 'second_review': True}. Separately, nothing consumes constraints.avoid_account: spawn.run_worker (spawn.py:214-225) derives `avoid` only from the reviewed execute task's account and never reads the review's own constraints, so even a non-None value would be ignored and both reviews deterministically land on the same non-executor account. Either re-read the task (bus.get(existing[0]['id'])) and honour the key in run_worker, or drop the dead field and say in pool.toml/README that both reviews share an account.

Step 7 still promises '7-10 cross-model adversarial', which the new Claude-executor branch makes false for the common case. gate() now puts BOTH reviews of a Claude-fallback-executed 7-10 task on review_tier(t) - one single tier - so a claude:opus-executed task is graded twice by sonnet and never cross-model. Confirmed by running gate(): tiers == ['sonnet','sonnet']. T-0150 item 3 asked to either route the second review off-model or 'drop the claim and state the tradeoff explicitly'; the docstring, pool.toml and README were reworded but the two governing docs were not. Identical stale line at .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md:15, which test_planner_md_matches_claude_md_lists keeps in lockstep, so both need the same edit.

`self.assertIn("avoid_account", reviews[1]["constraints"])` asserts only that the key exists; it passes against the always-None value the code actually produces, so the test cannot fail for the defect it was written to cover. Either assert the concrete account id (after making gate() re-read r1) or delete the assertion rather than leave a green test standing behind an inert field.

'complexity >= two_reviews_from spawns two' is now wrong for an orphaned result: reviews_expected() (daemon.py:305) returns 1 for any orphaned task whatever its complexity, and gate()'s orphaned branch opens exactly one review. The paragraph documents the two-review rule that item 1 just carved the orphaned exception out of, so a reader gets the pre-fix behaviour. One clause is enough.

result.summary: Items 1, 4, 5 fully resolved with meaningful tests; item 3 resolved in code but two docs still overclaim and the avoid_account plumbing is inert; item 2 only half-resolved - the all-reviews-failed case is still the same silent unbounded wait. Conflict resolution kept both D1 and D2 content (git diff 1b94384 2e32566 touches only the added [review] table and the Pipeline paragraph; T-0121's scout-cap line and scout.md/pool.toml limits untouched). `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon tests.test_goals -q` = 76 tests OK. reconcile_dead and the orphaned branch in gate() intact; no shell strings built from config.
